page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: It is not a protic acid
steps.mark_note: It is not a protic acid
lines: Boric acid, H₃BO₃, is not a protic acid.
A protic acid gives an H⁺ ion of its own,
and boric acid does not do this.
It is a weak monobasic acid that acts as
steps.why: The question is settled by the first sentence, so the answer must say plainly that boric acid is not protic, and then say what kind of acid it is instead.
common_mistakes: Calling H₃BO₃ tribasic because the formula carries three hydrogen atoms. It is monobasic.
Writing that it releases three H⁺ ions in water. It releases none of its own.
steps.memory_tip: Three hydrogen atoms in the formula and none of them given away: boric acid is monobasic, not protic.
steps.margin_note: Answer the question in the first line with the word not, then explain.

steps.label: It accepts OH⁻ from water
lines: Boric acid takes a hydroxide ion from a
water molecule, and the H₃O⁺ left behind
Here B(OH)₃ is the same substance as
H₃BO₃. Only one hydroxide ion is taken,
steps.why: The acidity is real, but its source is different: the H₃O⁺ comes from the water molecule that lost its hydroxide ion, not from the boric acid. Accepting a pair of electrons with that hydroxide ion is what makes it a Lewis acid.
common_mistakes: Writing the anion as [B(OH)₃]⁻. Boron takes a whole hydroxide ion, so the anion is [B(OH)₄]⁻ with four OH groups.
Leaving out the H₃O⁺. Without it the equation does not show why the solution is acidic.
steps.memory_tip: Boric acid takes OH⁻ and leaves H₃O⁺ behind. The acidity comes from the water, not from the boron.
steps.margin_note: The equation with [B(OH)₄]⁻ and H₃O⁺ is what shows the Lewis behaviour.

insider_note: The word not has to appear in the answer: a student who explains why the solution is acidic without saying that boric acid is not protic has answered a different question.
